items.title: The AI Skills Employers Now Expect from MBA Graduates
items.summary: Global employers are shifting their focus away from technical coding skills, choosing instead to evaluate business graduates on "managerial" AI competencies such as AI project management, organizational AI strategy, and translating data dashboards into sound business decisions.

items.title: Why Early-Career Talent Needs a Launchpad, Not a Slow On-Ramp
items.summary: As AI tools accelerate information synthesis for entry-level business staff, organizations are realizing that they must aggressively train early-career talent in subject-matter context and critical human judgment to prevent poor-quality, AI-generated outputs.

items.title: What AI Skills Do Employers Actually Look For in 2026?
items.summary: Surveys reveal that more than one-third of entry-level jobs now require basic AI competency—nearly triple the share from late 2025—with employers placing a heavy premium on non-technical skills like prompt engineering, workflow automation, and ethical AI judgment.

items.title: Where Is AI Creating the Most Demand for Business Administration Graduates?
items.summary: While AI is automating routine reporting and administrative scheduling, it is rapidly driving demand for business administration majors in high-growth hybrid roles like AI business analysts, supply chain coordinators, and technology implementation managers.

items.title: The class of 2026 hiring report: how AI is raising the bar on entry-level hiring
items.summary: A survey of hiring managers found that 48% would prefer to invest in AI tools rather than hiring and training a recent college graduate, creating a significantly higher entry threshold for business graduates entering the market.

items.title: Q1 AI Insights for Policy Makers: April 2026
items.summary: This report highlights that while AI is automating routine health administration tasks, it is rapidly generating new healthcare jobs centered on uniquely human strengths—such as judgment, organizational expertise, interpersonal skills, and clinical accountability—which are shifting the baseline skills required for new graduates.

items.title: Careers in Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare Workers
items.summary: There is a surge in demand for health science graduates with interdisciplinary training (combining clinical knowledge with machine learning and health data ethics) as physicians and hospital systems aggressively transition toward using AI-driven diagnostic and patient tracking tools.

items.title: Healthcare AI Hiring Trends 2026
items.summary: Driven by the rapid adoption of ambient scribing technologies, healthcare organizations are actively doubling their AI headcount, creating highly compensated, specialized career tracks like ambient clinical AI engineers, clinical AI product managers, and AI governance risk officers.

items.title: Health Education Technology Adoption Trends: Preparing for the AI Era
items.summary: With over 40% of health education and public health roles projected to integrate AI tools by 2028, graduates are urged to develop data interpretation and tool-management skills to qualify for modern, strategic health promotion and analytics roles.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: Wake Forest VP Andy Chan outlines how AI is driving a "reversal of value" in the job market, placing a massive premium on the strategic, critical thinking, and ethical reasoning skills of liberal arts graduates as rote technical tasks are automated.

items.title: Class of 2026 Workforce Outlook: Grads and AI Fluency
items.summary: Handshake's senior survey reveals that while AI-driven job anxieties remain high, humanities and business graduates are increasingly highlighting AI skills on their resumes, matching employers' growing expectations for AI-fluent entry-level hires.

items.title: Generative AI Jobs in 2026: Which Roles Are Growing, Which Are Dying
items.summary: The analysis reports that basic prompting has become a baseline literacy skill, opening high-paying career opportunities for non-coders—particularly humanities degrees—who pivot to roles like AI Product Management and AI Ethics Auditing to guide and secure models.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of English Degree Careers
items.summary: This report highlights how AI is reshaping the job market for English majors by automating low-level proofreading and style tasks but expanding advanced roles in high-stakes fields like AI content strategy, digital marketing narrative design, and technical writing.

items.title: Enrollment Shifts: From Computer Science to 'AI-Resistant' Fields
items.summary: Fueled by a Gallup-Lumina study showing widespread AI career anxiety, college enrollment is shifting away from computer science toward perceived "AI-proof" majors that emphasize human elements like empathy, ethics, and complex problem-solving.

items.title: Why the liberal arts can help young Americans prepare for the era of AI
items.summary: Career experts report that as generative AI automates routine programming and basic financial tasks, employers are placing a renewed premium on the emotional intelligence (EQ), critical thinking, and lateral problem-solving skills typical of social science majors.

items.title: AI Impact on Student Career Choices: Survey Reveals 4 in 10 Rethinking College Majors
items.summary: Data from the 2026 Gallup-Lumina State of Higher Education Study reveals that 42% of bachelor's degree students are reconsidering their majors due to AI's disruptive potential, prompting many to pivot from technical specialties toward "AI-resistant" social science and humanities fields that emphasize empathy and complex reasoning.

items.title: AI, Automation, and the Future of Sociology Degree Careers
items.summary: While routine coding and data entry roles face automation, AI is driving rapid job growth (exceeding 15% through 2032) in interdisciplinary career paths like social data analytics and AI ethics governance for sociology and social science graduates.

items.title: Impact of AI on Early
items.source: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
items.summary: Research on early-career workforce trends indicates that entry-level employees are increasingly tasked with directing and evaluating AI agents rather than performing routine execution, raising the workplace value of the critical reasoning and strategic problem-solving skills honed in social science programs.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: Career development leaders argue that as AI commodifies the mechanical "how" of work, there is a distinct reversal of market value back toward "strategic doers" with a "liberal arts brain" who possess the ethical and human context to decide the "what" and "why" of technological outputs.

items.title: Enrollment Shifts: From Computer Science to 'AI-Resistant' Fields
items.summary: Driven by fears of AI automation in entry-level coding, undergraduate computer science enrollment has dropped by 11% as students pivot toward hands-on, hybrid STEM paths like data science, physical engineering, and skilled trades.

items.title: DeepMind's CEO says STEM students can use AI 10 times more effectively
items.summary: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis argues that foundational STEM degrees remain invaluable, as students who master deep technical and architectural concepts will be able to operate AI tools far more effectively than those without technical backgrounds.

items.title: What AI Skills Do Employers Actually Look For in 2026?
items.summary: More than one-third of entry-level jobs now require basic AI competency—nearly triple the rate from late 2025—prompting an urgent need for STEM and non-STEM graduates alike to build practical skills like prompt engineering and workflow automation.

items.title: The Industries Hiring AI Talent in 2026
items.summary: The rapid adoption of AI has created a severe skills gap across diverse sectors like healthcare and manufacturing, leading employers to offer substantial wage premiums of up to 56% for STEM professionals who can successfully deploy AI models in domain-specific tasks.

items.title: What percentage of US college students have changed majors due to AI?
items.summary: A recent Gallup-Lumina study revealed that 42% of bachelor's degree students have seriously considered changing majors due to AI anxiety, prompting many to pivot from purely technical fields toward "AI-resistant" majors that emphasize emotional intelligence, physical dexterity, and complex human problem-solving.

items.title: Why the liberal arts can help young Americans prepare for the era of AI
items.summary: Career experts report that as AI increasingly automates technical execution and quantitative skills, employers are placing a higher premium on liberal arts graduates who possess the high-EQ, lateral thinking, and creative problem-solving skills that models cannot easily duplicate.

items.title: 11x survey shows Class of 2026 entering the workforce expect fewer entry-level roles, higher salaries, and stronger AI skills than their managers
items.summary: A survey of 1,000 business majors highlighted that while 80% believe AI is shrinking traditional, repetitive entry-level paths (like basic sales prospecting), graduates are proactively utilizing AI tools weekly to position themselves for newly emerging, high-value hybrid roles.

items.title: Where Is AI Creating the Most Demand for Humanities Graduates?
items.summary: While routine content creation is increasingly automated, a 30% surge in ethical AI development and digital media roles has opened new doors for humanities graduates skilled in ethical storytelling, bias mitigation, and human-centric design.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: Career development experts note that AI’s automation of everyday technical workflows has commodified the "how" of work, leading employers to heavily prioritize "strategic doers" with liberal arts backgrounds who bring critical thinking and ethical oversight to direct the "what" and the "why".

items.title: Report Highlights Changing Views on Skilled Trades
items.summary: According to a newly released report by Jobber, 68% of parents are rethinking the long-term stability of white-collar careers due to AI, with 38% stating that the rise of automation tools makes a career in the physical, skilled trades more appealing.

items.title: Gen Z Is Choosing Trade School as AI Threatens White
items.summary: As AI increasingly threatens entry-level office jobs, younger Americans are swarming trade schools to learn hands-on skills like electrical work, HVAC, and welding that chatbots or robots cannot easily replace.

items.title: ‘Job forever’: Trade schools in US all the rage in the AI era
items.summary: Trade school enrollment is booming in the United States as young adults seek career safety from AI disruption, while the physical construction of data centers to house AI technology simultaneously creates massive new demand for trade specialists like electricians.

items.title: Skilled Trades Survey 2026: How Gen Z Views AI & College
items.summary: A comprehensive survey of Gen Z adults revealed that 52% of current college students view skilled trades as safer from AI-driven disruption than office jobs, highlighting HVAC, plumbing, and electrical careers as highly insulated pathways.
